parsed.headline: Gaza rescuers report seven killed in separate Israeli strikes

pages.text: Gaza’s civil defense rescue service reported on Thursday that seven people were killed in separate Israeli strikes throughout the day. Six of the seven fatalities occurred in various parts of Gaza City, while one person was killed by Israeli fire southeast of Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza, according to the rescue service. The Israeli army told AFP that three of the targeted individuals were “military operatives in terrorist organizations,” though the military stated it was checking reports regarding the other four victims. Specific incidents in Gaza City included a drone strike on a car that killed two people, a drone attack on a tent in a displaced persons encampment that killed one person, an aircraft bombing of a residential building that killed a woman and a child, and artillery shelling that killed a woman, according to the rescue service, Al-Shifa hospital, and health officials.

parsed.headline: Man sentenced to six years for starting Ditch 2 wildfire in Saskatchewan, Canada

pages.text: Jason Halkett has been sentenced to six years in prison for starting the fire that became last year's Ditch 2 wildfire in northern Saskatchewan. Judge Jeffrey Lubyk handed down the sentence on Thursday in Montreal Lake provincial court. Halkett pleaded guilty earlier this year to arson causing damage to property.

parsed.headline: Supreme Court rules in favor of Sino Africa regarding Borteyman land in Ghana

pages.text: The Supreme Court of Ghana delivered a judgment on June 3, 2026, overturning a majority decision from the Court of Appeal dated March 27, 2025, regarding two parcels of land in Borteyman, also known as Nungua Farms, in Tema within the Greater Accra Region. The land, which covers approximately 328.877 acres, was the subject of Civil Appeal No. J4/44/2025. According to a public notice issued by Sino Africa Development Company Limited on October 8, 2026, the court declared legal title in favor of Sino Africa, though this is subject to the possessory rights of the first and second defendants, Royal Bell Investments Limited and Terraform Development Limited. Sino Africa's entitlement to recover possession is also subject to the claims of those two companies. 10/08/2026

parsed.headline: Former Syrian general accused of atrocities is protected in Lebanon by U.S. and Lebanese authorities

pages.text: A joint investigation by the BBC and NPR has found that Bassam al-Hassan, a former Syrian general and senior advisor to former President Bashar al-Assad, is living in Lebanon under the protection and financial support of American and Lebanese authorities. Hassan, who oversaw Syria's chemical weapons program and faces U.S. sanctions and international warrants for crimes against humanity, moved to Beirut following the collapse of the Assad regime in 2024. According to four anonymous sources familiar with the arrangement, Hassan is being bankrolled and protected due to his willingness to provide intelligence, including information regarding the 2012 abduction of American journalist Austin Tice in Syria. The BBC reviewed records of a meeting between Hassan, Lebanese security officials, and representatives from the FBI and CIA in which Hassan was offered residency, protection, and assistance with living needs. Sources stated that Hassan receives money through an intermediary to make the funds harder to trace. While officials from two branches of Syria's new government have expressed a desire to have Hassan returned to face trial, the BBC reports that U.S. authorities want him kept in Lebanon. The FBI declined to comment on the findings, directing inquiries to a previous statement regarding its focus on establishing facts around the Tice case.

parsed.headline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announces execution plan for Fort Hood shooter while making false claim regarding Barack Obama

pages.text: Speaking to influencer Jack Posobiec, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that Nidal Hasan, a former army psychiatrist, will be executed by firing squad. Hasan killed 12 soldiers and one civilian during an attack at Fort Hood in 2009. During the discussion, Hegseth falsely claimed that former president Barack Obama downplayed the 2009 attack by calling it “workplace violence” instead of terrorism, according to reporting by The Guardian World.

parsed.headline: United States to increase humanitarian assistance for Rohingyas in Bangladesh

pages.text: The United States has decided to increase financial assistance for the Rohingya population sheltered in Bangladesh, according to a report by BSS via The Financial Express Bangladesh. Eric Geelan, the Charge d'Affaires (CDA) ad interim at the US embassy, conveyed the decision during a courtesy call on Shama Obaed Islam, the State Minister for Foreign Affairs, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka on Thursday. The move is intended to reaffirm Washington's continued humanitarian support for the forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals as Bangladesh seeks international support to address the protracted Rohingya crisis and growing humanitarian needs.

parsed.headline: Researchers say Britons are not being fully informed about climate and nature crisis

pages.text: Researchers say the British government must be honest about the scale of threats posed by climate and nature breakdown, following a study of viewers of the People’s Emergency Briefing. According to the research, 93% of 13,000 people surveyed said the public is not being fully informed about the climate crisis and nature loss. Professor Lorraine Whitmarsh of the University of Bath, who led the research, stated that while most people are aware of some climate risks, the “second-order risks” regarding food supplies, national security, and impacts on the NHS are not as obvious. The briefing, which was held last November at Central Hall in Westminster, featured nine experts providing assessments on the changes required for the UK to adapt to a changing climate and ecological landscape. The event was described as a “first-of-its-kind national emergency briefing.”

The People’s Emergency Briefing was a crowdfunded film outlining threats to public health, the economy, and food security. It has been viewed by an estimated 185,000 people across more than 3,400 screenings. Of those surveyed, 87% said watching the film increased their motivation to act, and the film is associated with a “substantial shift” in environmental concern and understanding. Additionally, 89% of respondents stated the government should respond to the crisis with emergency-level mobilisation comparable to the second world war or the Covid-19 pandemic. Professor Mike Berners-Lee, chair of the National Emergency Briefing, noted that the public understood the Covid-19 threat when trusted with facts. The team is calling for a televised, primetime emergency briefing fronted by the prime minister and delivered by independent experts. The government has previously faced accusations of hiding information after refusing to publish a report from UK intelligence officers regarding the national security impacts of ecosystem collapse.
